executionHistory.summary: Filed BUG-061-011 against commit 6ad1e8c98ce6e1aa35df779306c6a8835db172be. Re-verified the defect from primary sources rather than assuming it: acceptance_test.go:1 is //go:build integration; go-integration.sh:53 enumerates four package trees with ./tests/eval/... absent; grep for 'eval' in that wrapper exits 1 with zero matches; a repository-wide grep for TestAcceptanceGate across tests/, scripts/, .github/, internal/ returns only the function definition and one echo line, so nothing invokes it. The four implicated paths are identical at HEAD and in the working tree. Root cause: a missing invariant between an explicit package allow-list and a build tag, asserted only by a source comment that cannot fail. Second, independent finding: no executed-assertion count is emitted anywhere in the repository in any form, so the Stage 1 exit criterion is unmet by construction and the fix is larger than the delivery plan's two-file estimate — realistic size is 5 files, 1 new. Designed the fix (untagged ExecutedAssertions + FormatGateMarker in harness.go, unconditional marker emission in acceptance_test.go, package + non-zero-count assertion + focused-run rule in go-integration.sh) and the adversarial regression (internal/deploy/eval_lane_contract_test.go, cases A1-A7, where A1 is the current file content and must be rejected). NO FIX IMPLEMENTED — artifacts and RCA only, by instruction. Every DoD item left unchecked.

rootCause: Two mechanisms with complementary intent and no link between them. tests/eval/assistant/acceptance_test.go opted OUT of the untagged unit lane via //go:build integration on the stated assumption that the tagged integration lane would pick it up. scripts/runtime/go-integration.sh selects packages by an explicit allow-list, not ./..., and was never extended to include ./tests/eval/... A build tag can only include a file inside a package that was already selected, so the opt-out executed and the opt-in did not. Nothing asserts the pairing, so the assumption printed in the file's own header went stale with no surface turning red. The failure mode of a missing test is silence.
scopeOfClaim: This gate measures assistant routing accuracy and capture-fallback coverage on an offline corpus using the harness's deterministic keyword classifier as a structural proxy for the production router. It does NOT measure corpus-grant enforcement. The D25/D28 grant holes carried by spec 108 are a separate axis and are NOT made measurable by fixing this bug.
